arxiv-1912-01452.title: Assessing the Robustness of Visual Question Answering Models Journal: International Journal of Computer Vision
arxiv-1912-01452.creator: Jia-Hong Huang, Modar Alfadly, Bernard Ghanem, Marcel Worring
arxiv-1912-01452.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Jia-Hong Huang, Modar Alfadly, Bernard Ghanem, Marcel Worring. Deep neural networks have been playing an essential role in the task of Visual Question Answering (VQA). Until recently, their accuracy has been the main focus of research. Now there is a trend toward assessing the robustness of these models against adversarial attacks by evaluating the accuracy of these models under increasing levels of noisiness in the inputs of VQA models.

arxiv-2106-03157.title: Self-Supervision is All You Need for Solving Rubik’s Cube
arxiv-2106-03157.creator: Kyo Takano kyo.takano@mentalese.co
arxiv-2106-03157.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kyo Takano kyo.takano@mentalese.co. Existing combinatorial search methods are often complex and require some level of expertise. This work introduces a simple and efficient deep learning method for solving combinatorial problems with a predefined goal, represented by Rubik’s Cube. We demonstrate that, for such problems, training a deep neural network on random scrambles branching from the goal state is sufficient to achieve near-optimal solutions.

arxiv-2202-12901.title: Jet Launching from Binary Neutron Star Mergers: Incorporating Neutrino Transport and Magnetic Fields
arxiv-2202-12901.creator: Lunan Sun, Milton Ruiz, Stuart L. Shapiro, Antonios Tsokaros
arxiv-2202-12901.description: Abstract We perform general relativistic, magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations of merging binary neutron stars incorporating neutrino transport and magnetic fields. Our new radiative transport module for neutrinos adopts a general relativistic, truncated-moment (M1) formalism. The binaries consist of two identical, irrotational stars modeled by the SLy nuclear equation of state (EOS).

arxiv-2211-16479.title: Approaches to the Parallelization of Merge Sort in Python
arxiv-2211-16479.creator: Alexandra Yang
arxiv-2211-16479.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexandra Yang. The theory of divide-and-conquer parallelization has been well-studied [ 1 ] in the past, providing a solid basis upon which to explore different approaches to the parallelization of merge sort in Python. Python’s simplicity and extensive selection of libraries make it the most popular scientific programming language, so it is a fitting language in which to implement and analyze these algorithms. In this paper, we use Python packages multiprocessing and mpi4py to implement several different parallel merge sort algorithms.

arxiv-2303-08274.description: Abstract Current point cloud segmentation architectures suffer from limited long-range feature modeling, as they mostly rely on aggregating information with local neighborhoods. arxiv-2403-15499.creator: Iman Emtiazi Naeini a {a}, Zahra Saberi b ∗ {b*}, Khadijeh Hassanzadeh c {c}
arxiv-2403-15499.description: Abstract This study employs the Causal Machine Learning (CausalML) statistical method to analyze the influence of electricity pricing policies on carbon dioxide ( CO 2 \text{CO}_{2} ) levels in the household sector. Investigating the causality between potential outcomes and treatment effects, where changes in pricing policies are the treatment, our analysis challenges the conventional wisdom surrounding incentive-based electricity pricing.

arxiv-2412-06853.description: Abstract This paper proposes a novel loss function called Tube Loss, developed for the simultaneous estimation of the lower and upper bounds of a Prediction Interval (PI) in regression problems, including probabilistic forecasting in autoregressive framework. The PIs obtained through empirical risk minimization using Tube Loss exhibit superior performance compared to those derived from existing approaches.

arxiv-2501-18705.title: Hyperbolicity, topology, and combinatorics of fine curve graphs and variants
arxiv-2501-18705.creator: Roberta Shapiro
arxiv-2501-18705.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Roberta Shapiro. Given a surface, the fine k k -curve graph of the surface is a graph whose vertices are simple closed essential curves and whose edges connect curves that intersect in at most k k points. We note that the fine k k -curve graph is hyperbolic for all k k and, for k ≥ 2 , k\geq 2, show that it contains as induced subgraphs all countable graphs.

pmc-11736341.title: 铁死亡相关基因热休克蛋白A5与肝细胞癌因果关系的孟德尔随机化和中介分析
pmc-11736341.creator: 兵 崔, 铖铖 许, 瑗 徐, 阿琴 陈, 朝明 毛, 跃华 陈
pmc-11736341.description: 目的探讨铁死亡相关基因热休克蛋白A5（HSPA5）与肝癌发展的因果关系及其作用机制。方法采用两步两样本孟德尔随机化（MR）设计评估HSPA5、调节性T细胞及肝癌之间的因果关系。首先通过公开的全基因组关联研究（GWAS）数据库筛选与HSPA5、调节性T细胞、肝癌相关的单核苷酸多态性作为工具变量，采用MR分析HSPA5对肝癌的直接影响，接着通过两步MR分析调节性T细胞在这一过程中可能的中介作用。同时，以肝癌为暴露因素，HSPA5为结局变量进行了反向MR分析。所有MR分析均以逆方差加权法作为主要的因果关联检验方法，通过MR-Egger、加权中值法、加权众数法和简单众数法验证结果的稳健性，并采用Cochrane’s Q统计量评估工具变量的异质性，MR-Egger回归的截距项和MR-PRESSO进行多效性检验，留一法进行敏感性分析。利用癌症基因组图谱（TCGA）数据库和人类蛋白质图谱（HPA）数据库验证HSPA5在肝癌组织中的表达水平及其与调节性T细胞的相关性，揭示HSPA5与调节性T细胞在肝癌进展中的相互作用机制及其与患者预后的关系。结果MR分析结果显示，HSPA5表达增加与肝癌风险呈正相关（均P<0.01），而反向MR分析未发现肝癌与HSPA5之间存在关联（P>0.05）。HSPA5表达与调节性T细胞功能显著相关（均P<0.05），且调节性T细胞在肝癌微环境中的富集与肝癌进展呈正相关（均P<0.05）。中介效应分析结果显示，调节性T细胞在HSPA5和肝癌间的中介效应分别占5.00%和7.45%。TCGA和HPA数据库分析显示，肝癌组织中HSPA5的mRNA和蛋白质表达水平均高于正常组织，且高表达与患者不良预后显著相关。免疫浸润分析验证了HSPA5与调节性T细胞之间的显著正相关性，且调节性T细胞在肝癌中的高浸润与肝癌进展密切相关。结论HSPA5的高表达与肝癌的发生及不良预后显著相关，并可能通过调控调节性T细胞在肿瘤微环境中的功能促进肝癌发展。 肝癌在全球范围内是导致癌症相关死亡的第三大原因，其发病率和病死率的持续上升对肿瘤学领域提出了严峻挑战［1］。尽管肝切除、肝移植、局部消融、介入治疗及免疫治疗等多种治疗手段已取得一定进展，但肝癌的整体治疗效果依然不尽如人意［2］，迫切需要深入研究肝癌的发病机制及发展治疗新方法。 近期，铁死亡作为一种新兴的非凋亡细胞死亡方式，通过依赖铁离子的脂质过氧化作用，在多种癌症特别是肝癌治疗中显示出潜在的应用价值［3-4］。研究发现，铁死亡不仅可以通过遗传及表观遗传学改变和代谢重编程促进肿瘤进展，还能通过激活特定免疫途径推动肿瘤发展［5-6］。HSPA5作为一种分子伴侣蛋白，对于内质网蛋白质折叠及压力减轻至关重要，影响癌细胞的存活和增殖［7］。已有研究指出，HSPA5与铁死亡的关键调节因子GPX4相互作用，会直接影响细胞在应激条件下生存与铁死亡的平衡，以促进结直肠癌的发展［8］。然而，HSPA5在肝细胞癌（以下简称肝癌）中的具体作用尚未明确。 MR是一种通过分析遗传变异来推断暴露因素与疾病结果之间因果关系的方法。MR分析的核心在于利用GWAS识别的与特定疾病密切相关SNP作为评估暴露和结果因果关系的工具变量。这种方法所涉及的遗传变异在减数分裂中随机分配，通常不受环境因素干扰［9］。本研究利用两步两样本MR方法，探讨HSPA5与肝癌之间、HSPA5与免疫细胞之间，以及免疫细胞与肝癌之间的潜在因果关系；通过两步MR分析进一步研究免疫细胞在HSPA5与肝癌关系中的中介作用，旨在为肝癌的发生发展机制提供新的见解并探索新的治疗靶点。 材料与方法 资料来源 eqtl-a-ENSG00000044574（HSPA5）数据来源于IEU OpenGWAS项目，肝癌实验组和验证组数据来源于芬兰数据库（FINNGEN_C3_LIVER_INTRAHEPATIC_BILE_DUCTS_EXALLC和FINNGEN_C3_BILIARY_GALLBLADDER_EXALLC），免疫表型的GWAS数据提取自GWAS目录（登录号从GCST0001391到GCST0002121）。 工具变量筛选方法 为确保MR分析获得可靠结果，必须满足以下三个关键假设：①选定的工具变量必须包括与HSPA5相关的独立SNP；②所有通过质量控制筛选的工具变量不应与混杂因素相关；③工具变量对HSPA5的影响必须仅通过与肝癌的关系来介导。对SNP进行质量控制，以满足MR分析的上述假设。首先，以全基因组显著性阈值P<5×10－8、P<5×10－6和P<5×10－8分别筛选HSPA5相关SNP、调节性T细胞相关SNP，以及肝癌相关SNP。其次，对HSPA5和调节性T细胞的SNP进行聚类处理，只保留独立的SNP。参考欧洲国际千人基因组计划数据，本研究进行了聚类的连锁不平衡分析（阈值设置为R 2<0.001，聚类窗口大小＝10 000 kb）［10］。再次，去除回文SNP，以确保SNP对HSPA5的影响与对肝癌的影响对应相同的等位基因。最后，使用F统计来排除弱工具变量（F<10）。具体公式为F=R 2（n－k－1）/k（1－R 2），其中R 2为由SNP解释的HSPA5方差，n为样本量，k为工具变量数。 MR分析方法 本研究采用两步两样本MR设计，评估HSPA5、调节性T细胞及肝癌之间的因果关系。首先通过MR分析测试HSPA5对肝癌的直接影响，再通过两步MR分析探讨调节性T细胞在这一过程中可能的中介作用，见图1。同时，为探讨肝癌对HSPA5的潜在因果效应，本研究以与肝癌相关SNP作为工具变量，HSPA5作为结局变量进行了反向MR分析。所有MR分析均以IVW作为主要的因果关联检验方法，并通过MR-Egger、加权中值法、加权众数法和简单众数法对结果进行验证。为提高结果的稳健性，实验组与验证组使用来自不同数据库的肝癌数据。 孟德尔随机化分析流程图 Flowchart of the mendelian randomization analysis HSPA5可通过不同途径对肝癌产生潜在影响. HSPA5对肝癌的整体影响为总效应；直接作用于肝癌发展为直接效应；通过免疫细胞间接影响肝癌发展为间接效应，分为间接效应1和间接效应2. MR分析的稳健性和可靠性检验 为确保MR分析结果的可靠性，本研究进行了异质性、多效性和敏感性分析。采用Cochrane’s Q统计量评估工具变量的异质性，P<0.05表示存在异质性；多效性检验通过MR-Egger回归的截距项和MR-PRESSO进行，其中MR-PRESSO用于检测并校正水平性多效性导致的离群值；敏感性分析采用“留一法”，以排除个别SNP对结果的影响，确保单一SNP不会显著影响HSPA5、调节性T细胞与肝癌之间的因果关系。 中介效应分析 采用中介效应分析探讨调节性T细胞在HSPA5与肝癌因果关系中的中介作用。各效应量的计算公式如下：总效应=C×100%，间接效应=A×B×100%，直接效应（C'）=（C－A×B）×100%，中介效应占比=A×B/C×100%。其中，A为HSPA5与免疫细胞MR分析的β值，B为免疫细胞与肝癌MR分析的β值，C为HSPA5与肝癌MR分析的β值。 临床资料验证 为进一步验证HSPA5与肝癌及调节性T细胞之间的相关性，本研究通过下载UALCAN数据库、HPA公共免疫组化数据库和TCGA数据库中的资料，分析了HSPA5 mRNA在所有肿瘤中的表达水平、HSPA5的mRNA和蛋白质在肝癌组织和正常肝脏组织中表达的差异、HSPA5与肝癌中调节性T细胞的相关性，以及HSPA5 mRNA表达与肝癌患者预后的关系。 统计学方法 所有分析均使用R软件（4.1.1版）进行。MR分析使用R软件包“TwoSampleMR”进行，通过OR量化HSPA5对肝癌的影响。统计学显著性水平设定为P<0.05。 结果 HSPA5与肝癌的关系 IVW分析结果显示，HSPA5与肝癌呈正相关（OR=2.0676，95%CI：1.3568~3.1505，P=0.0007），这种正相关性在验证集数据中同样可以观察到（OR=1.6406，95%CI：1.0147~2.6524，P=0.0434），且MR-Egger、加权中值法、简单众数法和加权众数法等分析结果与IVW分析结果方向基本一致，见表1。TCGA数据库分析显示，HSPA5在包括肝癌在内的大多数癌症中高表达（附图1）；在肝癌中，肝癌组织（n=371）和正常肝组织（n=50）中HSPA5 pmc-12615513.title: The impact of an extinction reminder on AAB renewal is sensitive to the level of association with extinction
pmc-12615513.creator: A Matías Gámez, Fátima Rojas-Iturria, Rodolfo Bernal-Gamboa
pmc-12615513.description: An experiment using a predictive learning task with college students evaluated the impact of a stimulus associated with extinction on an AAB renewal design. Four groups of participants learned a specific relationship between two cues (X and Y) and two outcomes (O1 and O2) in Context A during the first phase.

pmc-12655139.title: Translational Pharmaco-Nutritional Approaches in the Management of Clinical Acute Pancreatitis—A Narrative Review
pmc-12655139.creator: Muhammad Shamoon, Sara Alzaanin, Safia Naz, Paul N Smith, Rachel W Li, Predrag Sikirić
pmc-12655139.description: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is an inflammatory disorder of the pancreas that can lead to serious systemic complications. Its clinical presentation varies widely, ranging from mild, self-limiting symptoms to severe, life-threatening illness. Currently, there are no specific therapies approved for the treatment of AP, and management primarily relies on supportive care.

pmc-13183770.title: Challenging Anticoagulation With Warfarin and Heparin Following Mechanical Mitral Valve Replacement in a Patient With Infective Endocarditis: A Case Report Highlighting Diagnostic Difficulties
pmc-13183770.creator: Musawer Khan, Ayesha Ahmad, Moin Khan, F. N. U. Zainullah, Nauman Khan, Fatima Nazir, Wakil Ahmed, Naqeeb Ullah, Muhammad Anees, Kamil Ahmad Kamil
pmc-13183770.description: Warfarin remains the cornerstone of anticoagulation therapy following mechanical heart valve replacement. However, challenging anticoagulation responses, resistance to warfarin, and even more rarely to both warfarin and heparin pose significant clinical challenges and complicate management strategies. We describe a 44‐year‐old male with infective endocarditis who underwent mechanical mitral valve replacement.

pmc-13217763.title: Medical students’ attitudes toward patient safety and medical error reporting in Syria
pmc-13217763.creator: Aya Alkhdr, Ahmad Al-Bitar, Ibrahim Aljnide, Jawad Jalloul, Ali borji, M. Eyad Chatty
pmc-13217763.description: BackgroundPatient safety is a core competency in medical education, yet evidence from conflict-affected and low-resource settings remains limited. This study assessed patient safety attitudes among undergraduate medical students in Syria and identified predictors of overall attitudes and error reporting behavior.MethodsA multi-center cross-sectional survey was conducted among medical students from four Syrian universities using the Attitudes to Patient Safety Questionnaire-III (APSQ-III).

pmc-13603379.title: Patient-Specific Computational Fluid Dynamics of Pulmonary Arterial Hemodynamics in Dogs with and Without Pulmonic Stenosis
pmc-13603379.creator: Carla Zamora-Perarnau, Mauro Malvè, Patricia Sebastián-Marcos, Rocío Fernández-Parra
pmc-13603379.description: Simple SummaryPulmonic stenosis is a congenital heart disease caused by the narrowing of the pulmonary valve, leading to a flow obstruction between the right ventricle and main pulmonary artery. Although echocardiography and computed tomography are routinely used to diagnose this condition, they do not provide complete information about how blood moves through the affected vessels.

uslaw-usc-t20-s7371.title: 20 U.S.C. § 7371 — Prohibition against Federal mandates, direction, or control
uslaw-usc-t20-s7371.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t20-s7371.description: United States Code, Title 20 (Education); Chapter 70 (Strengthening And Improvement Of Elementary And Secondary Schools); Subchapter V (Flexibility And Accountability); Part C (General Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Nothing in this subchapter shall be construed to authorize an officer or employee of the Federal Government to mandate, direct, or control a State, local educational agency, or school’s specific instructional content.

uslaw-usc-t36-s104.title: 36 U.S.C. § 104 — Carl Garner Federal Lands Cleanup Day
uslaw-usc-t36-s104.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s104.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part A (Observances And Ceremonies); Chapter 1 (Patriotic And National Observances). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Designation.— The first Saturday after Labor Day is Carl Garner Federal Lands Cleanup Day. (b) Proclamation.— The President shall issue a proclamation calling on the people of the United States to observe Carl.
